purpose: Perindopril erbumine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and to reduce the risk of heart attack in people with heart disease. It can also help protect the kidneys in people with diabetes. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that causes your blood vessels to tighten and squeeze, which raises your blood pressure. This medicine blocks the enzyme that makes that chemical, so your blood vessels relax and widen. When your blood vessels are more relaxed, your heart does not have to work as hard and your blood pressure goes down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a dry, persistent cough that does not go away — this is very common with this type of medicine. You might also notice dizziness, especially when you stand up quickly, headache, feeling tired, or mild stomach upset. These effects are usually manageable, but let your doctor or pharmacist know if they bother you.
warnings: Stop taking this medicine and call your doctor right away if you notice swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, as this can be a rare but serious allergic reaction called angioedema. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Avoid taking it with potassium supplements or salt substitutes unless your doctor says it is okay, and be careful about getting dizzy or lightheaded when standing up.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 4 mg once a day, often taken in the morning. Your doctor may increase this to 8 mg once a day depending on how well your blood pressure is controlled. It can be taken with or without food, and it is best taken at the same time each day to help you remember.
